source.title: LLM Defenses Are Not Robust to Multi-Turn Human Jailbreaks Yet
source.authors: Nathaniel Li; Ziwen Han; Ian Steneker; Willow E. Primack; Riley Goodside; Hugh Zhang; Zifan Wang; Cristina Menghini; Summer Yue

record.file_problem: No major file problem; the text is readable, with minor OCR/encoding artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether attacks can elicit knowledge after RMU unlearning, using human multi-turn jailbreaks and automated attacks rather than the original unlearning-robustness evaluations.
record.gate_note: The relevant experiment applies RMU to LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and tests recovery on WMDP-Bio. Appendix C survey comments and the jailbreak examples are not separate measured results. The paper does not test fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or a counter-method.
record.test_reason: The study applies RMU to LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and measures whether prompting-only attacks recover WMDP-Bio knowledge. These are human multi-turn jailbreaks and six single-turn automated attacks, scored on 43 free-response questions. It also reports multiple-choice accuracy and MMLU after unlearning. No fine-tuning, internal-edit, quantization or counter-method experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that multi-turn human jailbreaks recover dual-use biosecurity knowledge from the RMU model and that current automated attacks are insufficient to assure RMU's robustness. They also note recovery was harder than on HarmBench despite unlimited time, and hypothesize domain expertise is needed. They caution against direct human-versus-automated ASR comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RMU, the method from the WMDP work, but applies it to LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct rather than the original Zephyr-7B-Beta and selects RMU hyperparameters through a search; it retains some stated hyperparameters from the cited work.
record.method_sensitivity: The unlearning experiment uses a different base model from the cited RMU work; for WMDP-Bio human red teaming, the team used unlimited time and 240 total hours, unlike the HarmBench pipeline.
record.code_released: not stated; the paper says model weights are publicly available at ScaleAI/mhj-llama3-8b-rmu and MHJ is released at https://scale.com/research/mhj
record.problems: WMDP-Bio uses 43 sampled questions converted to free response. Human red teaming had unlimited time and 240 total hours, and the paper notes the technical biosecurity domain may require specialized experience. No uncertainty estimates are reported. There is no attack-success comparison to a model that never saw the targeted knowledge, so the no-more-than-never-trained baseline in the claim is not tested.

untested.parts: Only RMU is tested, on one model. There is no attack baseline on the base model or on a model never trained on the knowledge. Recovery is not measured as multiple-choice accuracy.
No activation ablation or internal analysis.
Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information are not tested as separate conditions. They appear only as red-teamer tactics with no per-tactic ASR on WMDP-Bio.

missing.what: WMDP-Cyber multiple-choice accuracy before and after RMU (appears to be 46.6% to 28.0%).
85.7% of successful WMDP-Bio human jailbreaks needed more than one turn; the average successful submission took 20.5 minutes.

record.verdict_notes: The record used version codes V1/V5; these map to A and E. The study is not an original source, though its first author co-authored WMDP. Human and automated ASRs differ in threat model: humans had multi-turn access and unlimited time, and were graded manually. No ASR is reported for the base (non-unlearned) model, so recovery relative to the knowledge's original level is unknown. n=43 and no uncertainty is reported. The Appendix C red-teamer comments on RMU (gibberish on keywords, codeword substitution working) are qualitative only.

versions.untested_parts: It tests RMU's WMDP performance, MMLU retention, and attacks on the unlearned model. It does not test every unlearning method or compare attack recovery with a never-trained-on-knowledge model.
No fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery experiment.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-edit experiment.
Tests multi-turn human jailbreaks and automated attacks on RMU for WMDP-Bio, not rephrasing, languages, or in-context information as separate conditions.
No newer counter-method is tested for resistance to the attacks.

relation.reason: Reports attack recovery from an RMU-unlearned model, plus MCQ/MMLU after unlearning; bears on A and E.

tranche.reason: Applies RMU to Llama-3-8B-Instruct with its own hyperparameters and tests recovery by human multi-turn and automated prompting on free-response WMDP-Bio. This is a different test method on the same question.

source_check.notes: Shares 4 authors with the WMDP original (incl. first author Nathaniel Li); not an independent test. All values are figure-only (Figure 4 ASRs, Figure 8 MCQ/MMLU). The Figure 4 attack mapping follows legend order and fits the text's 39.6- and 25.6-point gaps. Figure 8 also seems to show WMDP-Cyber 46.6 -> 28.0, with no row. No base-model ASR. Human attackers had unlimited time and no biosecurity expertise; the authors caution against direct human vs automated comparison.
